data.description:
# Create an improved Phase Shift effect

## Problem statement

The current Phase Shift treatment — a static dark-blue desaturation overlay plus a
cyan/red chromatic split — is not distinctive enough: when the ship phases out the
player has to look for a subtle tint to confirm it, and enemies arriving out of the
wormhole carry no visual warning at all that they are "not fully here". The ask is a
"shimmer" and "glitch" read so a phased entity is unmistakably in a different state.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** "As a player, when my ship phases out — or when enemies
  emerge from the wormhole at the start of a wave — I want them to shimmer and glitch
  so it is instantly obvious they are not in their usual state."
- **Player (defensive read):** "As a player relying on the auto Phase Shift, I want the
  effect to visibly 'fire' at the moment of activation so I can trust it and time my
  flying accordingly."
- **Developer / maintainer:** "As a developer, I want the shimmer/glitch behaviour to
  live once in the shared core/VFX layer so the shipped game and every combat gym look
  identical and cannot diverge (gym↔game parity convention)."

Example user stories:

- *"My ship phased out mid-bullet-hell and I didn't even notice — I want the screen to
  ripple and shimmer the instant phase fires, then keep pulsing so I know the state is
  still on."*
- *"Scouts poured out of the wormhole and I couldn't tell they were materialising — I
  want each one to flicker and glow as it grows, so I read 'not solid yet'."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Player phase activation burst (glitch).** On the frame the Phase Shift activates (`isPhased` rising edge) the screen-wide treatment emits a brief **ripple/burst** — e.g. a short sharp chromatic-split surge with a flicker step — that reads as a "glitch" hit, distinct from the player-death juice (no camera shake; the existing screen-wide overlays are retained).
- **Continuous player shimmer while phased.** While `isPhased` stays true the treatment sustains a **continuous shimmer**: the existing cyan/red chromatic split becomes **more vivid and pulsing** — higher alpha (raised from 0.10 toward ~0.20), wider offset (raised from 3 px toward ~6 px) with a slow oscillation — plus a subtle alpha flicker (≈2–4 Hz) and a soft colour-pulse between the two split hues. All magnitudes exported as tunable constants with per-layer `PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*` toggles (mirroring the current `phaseShiftJuice` pattern). Phase expiry clears every layer on the falling edge, leaving no residual tint.
- **Per-enemy shimmer/glitch during wormhole emergence (no screen-space effects).** Each enemy growing from the wormhole gets a **per-entity** treatment over its growth window (`ENEMY_GROWTH_DURATION`): a brief ripple burst as it starts to materialise, then a continuous shimmer — a subtle scale/alpha flicker plus a soft colour-pulse on the entity itself — all driven from the shared spawn-animation path (`updateSpawnAnimation`) so `PlayScene` and every gym behave identically. No screen-wide overlay is introduced for the emergence path.
- **Wormhole-position glow/pulse ring.** While a wormhole is open for a wave the wormhole itself gets a subtle glow/pulse ring (radius pulse + soft glow at the wormhole position, drawn once per wormhole, tracked in the existing `wormholeEffects` registry and cleared when the wormhole closes). Visually distinct from both the phase-shift treatment and the player-death juice.
- **Tests and docs.** Unit tests cover: pure params model (new tunables mapped verbatim, toggles honoured), activation burst + continuous shimmer layer creation/teardown (edge-triggered, no residual layers), per-enemy shimmer driven by the spawn-state window, wormhole ring lifecycle, the no-camera-shake regression for Phase Shift, and safe-no-op behaviour headless. `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.2 (juice) is updated with the new shimmer/glitch treatment and tunables, and code comments document every new constant. The full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **No camera shake** (established producer decision — shake made Phase Shift read
  like player-death juice; the regression test asserting "never shakes" stays).
- **Gym↔game parity** (AGENTS.md): the shimmer/glitch behaviour lives once in the
  shared core/VFX layer (`src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`, `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`,
  the shared `CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene` spawn path) and is consumed by both
  `PlayScene` and the gyms — no divergent copies (duplicate-body guard + gym-parity
  docs assertion apply).
- **Screen-wide effects only for the player phase path.** The enemy-emergence path is
  per-entity/per-wormhole only — the producer explicitly chose "no screen space
  effects" for spawning enemies.
- Keep the existing cyan/red split identity (producer Q3 = A: more vivid, not
  recoloured); keep per-layer toggles and the pure `resolve*Params()` pattern.
- Safe no-op without a Phaser render context (headless tests); no new runtime
  dependencies; performance-neutral (tweens/alpha only, no per-frame allocations
  beyond the existing pattern).

## Existing state

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` — screen-wide Phase Shift treatment: dark-blue
  dim overlay (α 0.22) + cyan/red chromatic split (α 0.1, 3 px offset), edge-triggered
  `update(active, dt)` (the `dt` param is currently unused — reserved for pulsing).
  Camera-shake regression and pure-param tests in `phaseShiftJuice.test.ts`.
- `CombatCoreScene._updatePhaseShiftJuice(dt)` lazily constructs the controller and
  drives it from `getEffectsRegistry().isPhased` — shared by `PlayScene`,
  `GymFormationScene`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`.
- `applyPhaseGhost` (`CombatEffectVisuals.ts`) sets the ship ghost alpha while phased
  (unchanged; per-entity shimmer is additive and must not fight it).
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — wormhole open (1 s) → enemy growth
  (`ENEMY_GROWTH_DURATION` = 1.5 s via `startSpawnAnimation`/`updateSpawnAnimation`/
  `isEnemySpawning`) → close (0.5 s); `WormholeController` guarantees at most one live
  wormhole; `spawnWormholeOpen/Close` handles.
- `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` each drive spawn updates from `updateSpawnAnimation`
  and open/close the single wormhole from `this._wormhole` with the `wormholeEffects`
  registry (`CombatScene.wormholeEffects`, cleared on `SHUTDOWN`).

## Desired change

- In `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`: raise split alpha/offset and add a slow pulsing
  oscillation and an activation ripple/burst + continuous shimmer/flicker layer, all
  under tunables/toggles; keep edge-triggered apply/clear and the no-shake guarantee.
- In `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`: add per-entity shimmer/glitch helpers driven from the
  spawn-growth window (burst on growth start, then flicker/pulse while growing), and a
  wormhole glow/pulse ring tied to the wormhole's open lifetime.
- Wire the per-entity shimmer into the shared spawn path so `PlayScene` and the gyms
  consume it identically; wire the wormhole ring into the existing `wormholeEffects`
  registry lifecycle.
- Update `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.2 and code comments; extend the unit tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` — **Edit**: vivid/pulsing split, activation burst,
  continuous shimmer layers, new tunables/toggles.
- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.test.ts` — **Edit**: params, burst/shimmer, no-shake, edge
  trigger, teardown.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — **Edit**: per-enemy shimmer/glitch helpers +
  wormhole glow/pulse ring.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.test.ts` — **Edit**: new helper tests.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — **Edit (minimal)**: any
  shared wiring needed to drive the new effects (e.g. pass spawn state, ring
  lifecycle) without divergent copies.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — **Edit (minimal)**: consume the shared emergence-path
  helpers; no new behaviour.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — **Edit (minimal)**: consume the same
  shared helpers (parity).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — **Edit**: §7.2 juice description + new tunables.

## Risks and assumptions

**Risks**

- *Over-stimulation / seizure sensitivity* — shimmer, flicker and glitch bursts can be
  uncomfortable. Mitigation: keep magnitudes small and durations short, drive every
  layer from exported tunables with per-layer toggles (consistent with existing juice
  practice); player shimmer uses a gentle ≈2–4 Hz flicker, not rapid strobe; a
  reduce-motion accessibility option is out of scope here (separate tracked idea).
- *Player-death overlap* — the burst must not read as death juice. Mitigation: keep
  the no-camera-shake regression, reuse the chromatic-split identity only (never the
  death ring/flash palette), and keep the burst short (~150–250 ms).
- *Parity drift* — PlayScene/gym copies diverge. Mitigation: implement once in the
  shared core/VFX modules; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard and gym-parity docs
  assertion enforce this.
- *Per-frame cost* — pulsing/flicker must not allocate per frame. Mitigation: use
  Phaser tweens and existing object reuse; no new particle emitters beyond the ring.
- *Scope creep* — the "glitch" ask could balloon into post-processing shaders.
  Mitigation: keep to the current overlay/entity technique (no render-to-texture or
  shader work); record any shader-grade effect as a separate linked item.

**Assumptions** (producer-validated via Q1–Q3)

- *Player shimmer/glitch* = activation burst then continuous shimmer, **with** the
  existing screen-wide treatment retained and made more vivid/pulsing (producer: "for
  players D — with screen space effects"; Q3 = A).
- *Emerging enemies* = per-entity shimmer/glitch (burst + shimmer) **without** any
  screen-wide effect, plus a subtle wormhole-position glow/pulse ring (producer:
  "spawning enemies D — no screen space effects"; "B + wormhole effect — no screen
  space effects").
- The existing cyan/red split palette is retained (vivid, not recoloured).
- The ship's ghost alpha (`applyPhaseGhost`) is unchanged; per-entity shimmer is
  applied to emergent enemies only, not to the player's ship object itself.
- The effect is purely cosmetic: gameplay, hitboxes and spawn protection are
  unchanged.

## Related work

See the automated "Related work (automated report)" section below (added by the
`find-related` skill).

- Phase shift needs to be auto-applied when needed (AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8) — *completed*;
  parent of the existing automatic Phase Shift and its juice module.
- Phase Shift juice module (AH-0MUJRGWGG0073JWS) — *completed*; the module this work
  upgrades (screen-wide dim + chromatic split, no shake).
- PlayScene: add P6 phase-shift ghost visual (AH-0MU8QVC9Y008R8I5) — *completed*; the
  ship ghost-alpha precedent (`applyPhaseGhost`).
- Victory and defeat end-of-run fanfare (audio + visual juice) (AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB) —
  *completed*; reference for a layered, toggleable juice module and the defeat glitch
  flicker pattern.
- P6 charge and permanent auto-trigger model (AH-0MUJRGVQE004XA1T) — *completed*;
  introduced the Phase Shift auto-trigger the juice must clearly communicate.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — What specific visual effects should 'shimmer' and 'glitch' include?** Options:
  (A) rapid alpha flickering + colour cycling on the existing overlays; (B) screen-space
  distortion (pixel displacement / chromatic aberration wobble); (C) per-entity
  ripple/burst on activation + noise-like overlay flicker; (D) combination: brief
  ripple burst on activation, then continuous shimmer (flicker + subtle colour pulse).
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **D for spawning enemies (no screen space
  effects), D for players (with screen space effects).** Rationale: a brief burst on
  activation gives the 'glitch' hit, then a continuous shimmer maintains the state
  read; the agent's recommended option was D.
- **Q2 — Should enemies emerging from the wormhole receive the same screen-wide phase
  treatment or a per-enemy effect?** Options: (A) same screen-wide effect; (B) per-enemy
  personal shimmer/glow as it grows; (C) wormhole-position glow/pulse ring + standard
  screen-wide effect when phase-shift is active.
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **B + wormhole effect — no screen space
  effects.** Rationale: per-entity shimmer/glow during growth plus a subtle wormhole
  ring, with no screen-wide overlays on the emergence path.
- **Q3 — Colour palette/style for the shimmer/glitch?** Options: (A) keep the existing
  cyan/red split but more vivid (higher alpha, wider offset, pulsing); (B) purple/violet
  palette (wormhole colours); (C) neutral desaturated + subtle RGB-shift (CRT).
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A.** Rationale: preserve the established
  phase-shift identity while making it clearly more visible; the agent's recommended
  option was A.
